name: Alerts generated without recorded analysis or escalation criteria
description: Monitoring produces alerts, but the population lacks recorded dispositions, is exported filtered so the unanalysed backlog is hidden, or there are no documented criteria for when an anomaly becomes a security event.

may_assert: That alert records lack an analyst, disposition, or basis, where the alert export has been supplied.
That the export is filtered to escalated or closed items and so is not the alert population.
That no documented criteria distinguish an anomaly from a security event.
must_not_assert: That alerts were ignored. Absent records establish that analysis cannot be demonstrated, not that it did not occur.
That any specific analysis timeframe is required by SOC 2.
That an incident occurred or was missed.

escalates_to.when: A complete population positively shows alerts that passed their committed analysis timeframe with no disposition.
Alert volume is far beyond what the responder population could process, so detection exists without any realistic prospect of analysis.

severity_factors.criterion_impact: CC7.2 concerns analysing anomalies, not only generating them; unrecorded analysis leaves that half unevidenced.
severity_factors.pervasiveness: A few auto-closed low-severity alerts differ from a period with no dispositions at all.
severity_factors.detectability: Visible directly in the alert export, provided it is unfiltered.
escalates_when: No analysis timeframe or responder is defined anywhere
de_escalates_when: Auto-closure follows a documented suppression rule with a recorded basis
Analysis records live in a ticketing or incident system and reconcile
Alert volume is low and each item has a disposition

detection_signals.signal: Alert records lack analyst identity or disposition.
Export limited to escalated or closed alerts rather than the full population.
No documented criteria distinguishing an anomaly from a security event.
Respondent identifies no named responder, analysis timeframe, or escalation criteria.

auditor_impact: Auditors commonly sample alerts and ask what was concluded about each. Where analysis is recorded in a different system this resolves quickly; where it is recorded nowhere it tends to become reportable.
customer_impact: The vendor can show it collects telemetry but not that anyone assesses what it surfaces.
false_positive_guidance: Classified as insufficient evidence, not an operating gap. Absent records do not establish that analysis did not happen; request them first.
Not a gap where auto-closure follows a documented suppression rule with a recorded basis; that is informed triage at scale.
Not a gap where analysis is recorded in a ticketing or incident system rather than the alerting platform; reconcile across systems before concluding.
A low alert count is not itself a finding. Corroborate against EV-LOG-001 coverage before treating quiet as either healthy or broken.
Overlaps deliberately with FND-ENDPOINT-002, which covers the malware-specific detection population. Report one, not both, where the same records are in question.

source_refs.supports: Typical auditor treatment, severity factors, and detection approach.

notes: DriftGuard finding archetype. DriftGuard produces observations against it; only a service auditor issues findings.
